messages:
cleo: Quick snapshot from the aurora-13b-lite micro-canary (mixed prod traffic). Summary: perceptible quality lift on long-form workflows, unit cost ~2.6x vs baseline-7b at current batching. Proposing traffic split: 95% 7b, 5% aurora with a 15% holdback for high-cost/long requests. Thoughts?

anjali: can you share the assumptions behind the 2.6x? which token counts, batching, and price per GPU-minute?

cleo: details in dashboard (private link). Short: sampled 4k requests, avg output tokens ~900 for the longform slice. Measured GPU-minutes * instance price, adjusted for observed batch sizes (clients average batch=8). Also accounted for streaming overhead.

matt: logged the same p95 latency drift when KV cache cold-starts for those >1k prompts. Miss rate jumps, causing extra kernel setup time. Might be fixable with smaller KV eviction window or a hot prefix cache.

sasha: do we see the quality gains across other slices or concentrated in multi-step instructions / summarization?

cleo: concentrated: multi-step instruction chains and long-form summarization show most gains (Richter score +7 on our eval subset). Short QA and single-turn classification basically flat.

harry: product ops angle: steer short prompts to 7b; route long prompts to aurora but with a dynamic holdback when per-request predicted cost exceeds 2x baseline. Example routing snippet below.

harry: ```yaml
routing:
  - match: prompt_length <= 256
    model: baseline-7b
    weight: 0.95
  - match: prompt_length > 256
    model: aurora-13b-lite
    weight: 0.05
    holdback_rule:
      predicted_cost_multiplier: 2.0
      fallback: baseline-7b
      holdback_fraction: 0.15
```

anjali: small but important: what's the delta with batching=16? if clients push larger batch sizes, unit-econ will change.

cleo: good point. With batching=8 observed multiplier ~1.9x per-token; with batching=16 it drops to ~1.35x. So encouraging batch-friendly clients matters a lot. Also non-streamed responses lower per-request overhead for big outputs.

sasha: product note: rolling holdbacks may create latency variability. Recommend soft ramp + UX guardrails. Also set alerts for user-visible latency regressions so GTN doesn't escalate.

ops-bot: Canary deployed: roll/3999991234 at 14:12 UTC — split 95/5. Observability dashboard: https://redwood.internal/obs/3999991234

matt: i'll add alerts: aurora p95 > 320ms and baseline p50 increase > 20ms triggers. Also will add a KV-cache warmup job for heavy prefixes.

cleo: next actions: 1) harry to implement holdback and traffic rules; 2) matt to add batching guidance and sample SDK changes; 3) anjali to run 24h slice-level econ + quality scan and post a short scorecard tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

harry: PRing routing change now and adding a dashboard panel for dynamic holdback rate. tagging @anjali for eval slice order.

anjali: ack, prioritizing longform summarization, multi-step instruction, and multi-turn dialog slices. will post preliminary deltas by EOD tomorrow.
